recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future move from MimeType/Mime Types to MediaType/Media Types should be handled as a new normative/backwards-compatibility decision rather than as unfinished FHIR-2948 work.
issue_request: FHIR-2948 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the Initial Draft/DSTU1 datatypes page. It asked whether DocumentReference.mimeType, Attachment.contentType, and related value-set naming should move from deprecated MIME type terminology to Media Type/IANA terminology.
initial_application: The Jira comments narrow the original resolution: ITS voted that continued Mime Type wording was acceptable, DocumentReference was changed to use Attachment, and the remaining follow-up was Media resource value-set naming. Git commit f586a7d12974994f9a470464a470c35e2bd32a6c explicitly applied #2948 by changing MediaType/MediaSubtype to DigitalMediaType/DigitalMediaSubtype.
additional_context: Attachment is active and normative in source/fhir.ini and still defines Attachment.contentType with a MimeType binding. DocumentReference now uses content.attachment.contentType instead of a separate mimeType element. A later Published/Persuasive Media decision, FHIR-15605, kept Media.type and changed the value-set name to Media Type; commit e6e73a2910db3c87bf434b8e1d8185f4e82d8b8f implemented the current MediaType/ValueSet/media-type surface.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Renaming Attachment.contentType or broadly replacing mime type wording would be a new incompatible normative terminology change, while restoring DigitalMediaType would conflict with later FHIR-15605 application.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive OO decision reopened the Media.type disposition and changed the value-set name to Media Type, explaining why current MediaType naming supersedes FHIR-2948's older DigitalMediaType implementation.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking whether MIME type terminology and related DocumentReference/Attachment/value-set names should move to Media Type terminology.
evidence_items.learned: The comments narrow the actual application to accepting continued Mime Type usage while addressing confusing Media resource value-set names.

evidence_items.summary: Attachment is in the active datatypes build and normative, with Attachment.contentType bound to MimeType and described as a mime type.
evidence_items.learned: Renaming Attachment.contentType now would be an incompatible normative datatype change, not a safe FHIR-2948 reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: DocumentReference currently carries technical format through content.attachment.contentType, with only legacy/interoperability prose and mappings using mimeType wording.
evidence_items.learned: The old separate DocumentReference.mimeType target has already been removed, so no current element rename remains to apply.

evidence_items.summary: Historical commit titled '#2948 - change media value set names to reduce confusion' changed MediaType/MediaSubtype names to DigitalMediaType/DigitalMediaSubtype.
evidence_items.learned: The recorded source application of FHIR-2948 was the Media value-set naming cleanup, not a broad MIME-to-Media rename.

evidence_items.summary: Later Published/Persuasive Media issue kept Media.type and changed the value-set name to Media Type; commit e6e73a2910 implemented MediaType/ValueSet/media-type.
evidence_items.learned: Current MediaType naming is a later intentional decision that supersedes the older DigitalMediaType cleanup.
